word_for_word_source.work: FolioCorpus, English Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam word-for-word edition as displayed in the sreegd/shastra-folio public archive
word_for_word_source.file_index: one blob and SHA-256 per linked row of VERSE_SENSES.tsv
word_for_word_source.field: cr-syn-iast and its associated cr-syn-en in the same cr-syn-item; linked Sanskrit passage from cr-iast-line.

comparison_method: Carry the GRETIL verse, original token and previously adjudicated citation form. Confirm that the word-for-word column actually has that same Sanskrit lemma and that the surrounding Sanskrit matches its counterpart. Joined words and grouped verses use their stated editions. A nearby numbered verse with the same lemma is insufficient. The numeric overlap of normalized Sanskrit character 7-grams is recorded only as a collation diagnostic, not as evidence for a meaning. Each of the 112 retained pages is distinct.
source_scope: The semantic headings summarize one word-for-word gloss tradition. The free translation, the Sanskrit commentator, and other traditions may make different contextual choices. The observations do not generalize the root-vowel rules of the Puruṣakāra to every construction.
construction: For a grammar reading retain the preverb chain, root-vowel length, finite or participial ending or absolutive suffix, source verse, case/pada and the lexical gloss receiver. Projection may coincide for a hearing or a seeing selection; no deterministic reverse lookup from the long or short vowel distinguishes all possibilities.
